title: Quantitative (q)PCR and Differential Expression Analysis
author: Jeffrey A Lewis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbgpijvn
materials: Adjust volume to 7 μl with RNase-Free TE.
Analyze concentration via Nanodrop or Qubit.

1. Design qPCR plate layout using only the interior 60 wells. Do not use the outer edge wells of the PCR plate for your samples (no RT controls are okay), because uneven heating and/or evaporation increases variability. That means there are 60 usable wells for samples per PCR plate. 2. Dilute each primer to 10 μM. 3. Dilute each cDNA sample 5-fold (e.g. if you are using 1 ng cDNA per reaction, dilute the cDNA to 0.2 ng / μl). cDNA concentration should be based on primer efficiency testing (Step 3), using a concentration within the linear range of the assay. One ng of cDNA per qPCR reaction tends to work well for the majority of genes. When making cDNA dilutions, prepare a large enough volume so that you are pipetting no less that 2 μl of cDNA. Pipetting volumes smaller than 2 μl will decrease the accuracy of your dilutions. (E.g. 2 µl (1 ng / µl) cDNA to 8 µl of water for a 0.2 ng / μl dilution). 4. Prepare a qPCR Mastermix for each primer pair (N+1). For each reaction you will add the following amounts: 0.4 μl Forward Primer (final concentration 200 nM) 0.4 μl Reverse Primer (final concentration 200 nM) 4.2 μl water 10 μl Maxima 2X SYBR Green Mix (1x final) 5. Pipette 5 μl diluted cDNA to the bottom of the appropriate wells of a BioRad RT-PCR plate. Be careful not to touch the tips to the side of the wells. Use a single pipette tip for pipetting the same cDNA sample into multiple wells. 6. Pipette 15 μl qPCR Mastermix to the side of the appropriate wells. Use a single tip for each mastermix. Change tips when switching to a new mastermix (different primers). Be careful to only touch the side of the well so as to not contaminate the pipet tip with cDNA already in wells. 7. Seal qPCR plate with clear Bio-Rad sealing membrane; use roller if applicable. 8. Briefly spin the plate in a microplate centrifuge. This ensures all the qPCR mastermix reaches the cDNA in the bottom of the well. 9. Reaction conditions will be primer specific. Based on a primer Tm of 58°C we use the following cycling conditions: 95°C x 3 min ----------------------------------- 95°C x 15 sec 55°C x 1 min 40 cycles ----------------------------------- Melt curve analysis (55°C - 95°C in 5 sec steps; default instrument settings) Melt curve analysis allows us to check for co-amplification of non-specific products. More than one peak can indicate more than one PCR product, which should be verified via gel elecrophoresis on those samples. 10: Use the following instrument settings: Cq determination mode = regression Baseline settings = Baseline subtracted by curve fit with no fluorescence drift corrected Analysis mode = Fluoropore

ΔΔCt Analysis The critical threshold cycle (Ct - also labelled as Cq on Bio-Rad instruments) is the cycle number where the fluorescence signal crosses a set threshold. Differences in Ct values between samples can be used to measure relative transcript abundance. We use the ΔΔCt method to quantify difference in relative trancript abundance, as described by Livak and Schmittgen ( Methods. 2001. 25(4): 402-408.). This method assumes that both target and control (reference) genes are amplified with efficiencies near 100% and within 5% of each other (i.e. Step 3). 1. Normalize the Ct values by subtracting the Ct for your control gene from the Ct of the target gene. ΔCt (sample) = Ct (target gene) - Ct (control gene) 2. Calculate the ΔΔCt using the normalized values from step 1. ΔΔCt = ΔCt (treated sample) - ΔCt (untreated sample) Therefore: ΔΔCt = [Ct(target gene, treated) - Ct(control gene, treated)] - [Ct(target gene, untreated) - Ct(control gene, untreated)] To convert ΔΔCt to fold changes, use the following equation: 2 (-ΔΔCt)

steps.title: Design Primers
steps.instruction: Use Primer3 to design primers with a Tm as close to 58°C as possible and an expected product size of ~100 - 200 bp. For gene expression analysis, design primers within the 3' end of an ORF.

steps.title: Prepare RNA/Primer Mixture
steps.instruction: Combine RNA and primers, adjust volume, and denature.

substeps.instruction: Mix 10 μg total RNA with 3 μg anchored oligo-dT (T20VN) and 3 μg random hexamer (optional; use random hexamer for non-coding RNAs and prokaryotic mRNAs, or oligo-dT alone for poly-adenylated eukaryotic mRNA).
Adjust the total volume to 7 μl using RNase-Free TE.
Denature the mixture at 70°C for 10 min, then immediately chill on ice for > 2 min.

steps.title: Prepare Reverse Transcriptase Master Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a Master Mix for the number of samples plus one to ensure sufficient volume.

substeps.instruction: Combine 3.0 μl 5x Superscript Buffer, 1.5 μl 0.1M DTT, 3.0 μl 10x RNase-Free dNTPs (2.5 mM stock solution, final concentration of 250 μM), and 0.5 μl Superscript III RT.
For no RT control reactions, substitute Superscript III with an equal volume of RNase-Free water.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Combine the Master Mix with the denatured RNA and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Add 8 μl of Reverse Transcriptase Master Mix to the denatured RNA.
Incubate on bench (25°C) for 7 min (this step can be skipped if using oligo-dT alone).
Incubate at 50°C for 2 hrs in a thermal cycler.

steps.title: Clean and Concentrate cDNA
steps.instruction: Stop the reaction and purify the cDNA.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 μl 1 M NaOH and 10 μl 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) to each reaction.
Incubate at 65°C for 15 min.
Perform cDNA cleanup using Zymo Clean and concentrator (D4014) per manufacturer's instructions, adding the eluate back onto the column and repeating the elution to increase yield.
Analyze cDNA concentration via Nanodrop or Qubit.

steps.title: Validate Primer Specificity
steps.instruction: Perform PCR on genomic DNA from wild-type and deletion strains to verify specificity.

substeps.instruction: Run PCR using Taq polymerase with the following cycling conditions: 95°C for 3 min, then 30 cycles of (95°C for 15 sec and 55°C for 1 min).
Perform gel electrophoresis (2% agarose, ~120V for 30-60 min).
Verify a single band (100 - 200 bp) for wild-type and no band for the deletion strain.

steps.title: Determine Primer Efficiency
steps.instruction: Perform a standard curve analysis using a range of cDNA concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Dilute cDNA from a sample with known expression to 0.01 ng, 0.05 ng, 0.1 ng, 1 ng, 5 ng, 10 ng, 25 ng, and 50 ng (adjust range if using random hexamer).
Perform qPCR on the test gene and control gene across these concentrations.
Determine Ct (Cq) values for each concentration.
Log 10 transform the cDNA concentrations.
Plot Ct-values (y-axis) against log 10-transformed concentrations (x-axis) to ensure the data falls within the linear range; repeat dilutions if necessary.
Perform linear regression to calculate the slope and r² (typically close to 0.99).
Calculate efficiency using the equation: Efficiency(%) = (10^(-1/slope) - 1) x 100.
Ensure efficiencies are >90% and within 5% of each other for all primer pairs.
